title: Bhakti yoga: the nine forms of devotion; the Alvars and Nayanars; Mirabai, Tulsidas, Surdas; kirtan as method (7 of 7)
hook: a man in Bengal leads the whole town singing through the streets, and it becomes a method
tomorrow: Jnana yoga: neti neti in practice; Shankara's method; the Ashtavakra Gita opening (1 of 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Tulsidas the servant of Rama, and Surdas's toddler with butter on his face. Your line: love as the road. Today, the last day of bhakti, the end of the week, and the thing you can do together. Day two hundred seventy-three.

Maybe you've heard it at a temple, a yoga studio, or on a city sidewalk. One voice sings a line. Everyone sings it back. Drums, little hand cymbals, sometimes a harmonium wheezing along. The same few names, over and over, a little faster each time, until people who walked in stiff and shy are swaying, eyes closed, some of them crying. It can look like a concert. It's older than that, and it's meant as a method. Today: kirtan.
screen: `ONE VOICE, THEN EVERYONE.` → `DRUMS, CYMBALS, HARMONIUM.` → `NOT A CONCERT. A METHOD.`

segments.voice: Kirtan comes from the Sanskrit kirt: to mention, to tell, to praise aloud. It's the second of the nine forms of devotion. The Alvars and Nayanars sang. Mira sang. Surdas sang. But in Bengal, Chaitanya of Nabadwip turned singing into a movement. He would lead crowds through the streets, singing the names of Krishna, dancing, arms raised. Tradition says that when the local authorities tried to ban the public singing, he answered by organizing an even bigger procession. For Chaitanya's followers, the Gaudiya Vaishnavas, singing the divine name isn't a warm-up for devotion. It is the devotion. God, they say, is present in the name. Why does it work as a method? It's call and response, so you don't have to know anything; you just repeat. It uses the body: breath, voice, rhythm. It's done together, so your shyness gets carried by the group. And it runs on repetition, which, people who sing it say, slowly quiets the part of the mind that keeps commentating. That's this whole week. The nine doors, one room. Andal's garland and the singer on the priest's shoulders. Kannappa's eye. Mira's cup of poison. Tulsidas the servant, Surdas's toddler. And now a whole street singing. Bhakti says the road to God can be love, all the way. Tomorrow, the third path, which asks a very different question.
screen: `KIRT — TO PRAISE ALOUD.` · `CHAITANYA SINGING IN THE STREETS.` · `THE NAME IS THE DEVOTION.` · `CALL, RESPONSE, REPETITION.` · then, large: `LOVE AS THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: Sit, and try the shape of kirtan, even alone. Pick one short name or word that means something to you. If you pray, it can be a name of God: Rama, Krishna, Shiva, Om. If not, a word like peace, or a loved one's name. Say it softly on the out-breath. Then hear it, in your head, as if a room answered back. Say. Hear it return. Let it get slower, not faster. Let the commentary quiet. The bell holds the time.
Bhakti yoga, part seven: kirtan, singing the divine name together, call and response. For Chaitanya's followers, the name itself is the devotion.
Your line: love as the road. Today, sing something with someone, a car song, a lullaby, a birthday song, and notice what happens when two voices become one. Day two hundred seventy-three.

howItsDone: Kirtan is sung in temples, homes and public processions across the Hindu world: a leader sings a line of divine names and the group answers, usually with drums (mridanga), small cymbals (kartal) and harmonium; Gaudiya Vaishnavas, including ISKCON, make chanting the name central to daily practice.

original.note: Sanskrit: kirtana, praising aloud; from kirt, to mention, tell, praise.

trapdoor: what you thought: kirtan is a kind of concert.
what it means: kirtan is a method of devotion: call-and-response singing of divine names, done together.

what a scholar hears: in Gaudiya Vaishnava theology the name (nama) is non-different from Krishna; the movement around Chaitanya made nagara-sankirtana, congregational street singing, its signature practice.
